reflection.comment: The intentionally dynamic examples: methods without @Executable are invoked through the reflective resolvers of the specification, and MethodExpression.getMethodInfo has a java.lang.reflect contract.
A bean without an introspection: every one of its methods resolves through jakarta.el.BeanELResolver.

An expanded variable arity call is left to the reflective resolver, because BeanMethod does not carry the variable arity flag; the fixed arity executables of the type still go through the introspection.
Invoked statically through an imported class, jakarta.el.StaticFieldELResolver.
Invoked inside a stored lambda, where the method of the java.lang.String argument resolves reflectively.
A method expression over a list: the method is found on the interface, and the immutable implementation is the class the resolver reflects on.
A LambdaExpression is coerced to a functional interface with a dynamic proxy, section 1.25.8 of the specification: one stored in a variable, and one passed as the argument of a method.
A lambda coerced to the interface is a proxy standing in for it, and a default method on it reaches InvocationHandler.invokeDefault, which looks the proxy class up.
Neither introspected nor a bean, so the expression reaches it through the reflective resolver, which is what the scenario is for.

MethodExpression.getMethodInfo and getMethodReference describe a method through an executor rather than reflectively, and the annotations they report are synthesized as a proxy of the annotation type.
The default method of the coerced interface reaches InvocationHandler.invokeDefault, which needs the interface itself, not only the proxy of it.
The annotations a method expression reports are synthesized as a proxy of the annotation type.
The method deliberately left without @Executable, which the reflective resolver of the chain invokes.
